Notes: - Garlic oil and batter used for frying fish are Time /Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) and must be held at 41F or below or 135F or above at all times. Facility may use Time as a Control (TAAC ) for these items. TAAC procedure form included with inspection report . TAAC may be used under the following conditions: 1. Written procedures must be on site describing your process . 2. List the food that will use Time as a Control . 3. All food must be labeled with the time it will be discarded (no longer than 4 hours). 4. Food must be discarded by 4 hours and not saved for any purpose. If the food is found without a label or improper label, the facility is not in compliance. - Store utensils used for TCS foods at 41F or below, 135F or above, or in a clean dry location and wash, rinse, and sanitize every 4 hours. Compliance Schedule OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS You must complete the following items by the due date listed below . Your inspector will do a compliance inspection . If these items are not corrected, you will be billed for the inspection. Violations cited must be corrected within the time frames specified . Complete ByItem Number 07/30/2026 2600 Compliance with valid permit; operating and risk control plans and required written procedures. 2600 Facility has resumed using the ice machine and mixer. Facility is currently in plan review to use the equipment, but has not received a preopening inspection. Per your approval letter, " We have received notification that the plumbing system is not in compliance with City regulations. The preopening inspection cannot occur until you provide written documentation that all plumbing requirements have been met. You must receive a preopening inspection and written approval from the Health Department before using equipment or beginning operations that are currently in Plan Review. Call 253-649-1706 if you need assistance. Stop using the unapproved equipment. Submit FOG compliance verification from the City of Tacoma to food @tpchd.org and schedule your preopening inspection. Plan review stale date has been extended to 8/20/2026. *Compliance order issued to stop using unapproved immediately. Failure to stop will result in a fee of $240 for non-compliance. Contact your inspector with questions or if you need more time to complete these items. Due to 35 or more red points, a follow-up inspection will be conducted for the red item violations noted in this inspection report. A fee of $240 will be assessed by mail for all follow-up inspections. If repeated red item violations are observed at a follow-up inspection, an additional follow-up inspection will be required. Notes: - Hand sanitizer may not be used in place of washing hands. - Spatula used for raw eggs should be designated for raw eggs only. Both the handle and metal piece are contaminated after the employee handles raw shell eggs unless hands are washed first. After handling the spatula, employees must wash their hands before putting on gloves and/or handling ready to eat food or food contact surfaces. - Do not prepare matcha or store utensils below the handwash sink sink paper towel dispenser. Food and food contact surfaces must be protected from contamination at all times during storage, preparation, and display. If food prep is observed within 18 inches of the handwash sink during future inspections, facility will be required to move the paper towel dispenser and add a splashguard at least 12 inches tall, made of smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable material. - Inspector recommends obtaining 2-inch hotel pans for cooling cooked onions. If deeper pans are used, do not fill them deeper than 2 inches until the food reaches 41F or below. - Remove the pest spray from the facility. If pests are observed, use traps stored below and away from food and food preparation surfaces or a professional pest service. - Maintain a copy of the facility's Certified Food Protection Manager certificate on site for inspector review.
